content.text: I've reviewed the definitions, license grant and restrictions, commercial/fee articles, and the Article XXII "Right of First Refusal". No exclusive-dealing or sole-supplier covenant binds us anywhere.

input.quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: it imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation on us. The grant is expressly "non-exclusive" in both directions (p0030, p0043, p0049), and the Article II restrictions (p0035–p0047) are ordinary scope/anti-sublicensing limits on how we use the Licensed Technology — they do not stop us from licensing or using any other FX trading platform, ECN or liquidity source. The fee articles are usage-based on volume actually "traded with the Licensed Technology" (p0070) with no minimum-volume or all-flow-routing commitment, so there is no de facto exclusivity. The Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139) is a ROFR over a third-party offer to buy our assets or merge with us — a change-of-control/transfer constraint, not a procurement exclusivity — so it is out of scope for this rule and better addressed under the change-of-control rule (it also overlaps the Article XX consent right at p0134). The only other "exclusive" references are the Field of Use definition's "exclusive purpose" (p0007, a scope limit), the exclusive-jurisdiction clause (p0146), and the non-exclusive-remedy clause (p0142) — none creates exclusive dealing. No redline required.
